newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. guard punched and injured by intruder.
newsitem.headline: U.N. guard punched and injured by intruder.

text.p: A U.N. security guard was punched twice in the face on Thursday by an unidentified man trying to enter the United Nations compound, according to U.N. officials.

The guard, Richard Allyne, 52, was taken to nearby Lenox Hill Hospital for a contusion in his eye. He had wrestled the attacker to the ground despite the blows to his face, spokesman Juan-Carlos Brandt said.
Staff entering the building on New York's East River called for reinforcements and the man was handcuffed by other U.N. guards and then turned over to New York police.
Brandt said the attacker "spoke very little English" and was not associated with the United Nations.

The man had attempted to enter through a gate reserved for U.N. staff and others who have permanent passes. When asked to produce his identification card, "the individual punched Officer Allyne twice in the face," a U.N. statement said.
The United Nations said it would press charges against the assailant.
